ratings.why: Pressing Cancel on one task stops a different running task, which destroys work the user meant to keep and breaks the requested keyboard use.
The request says writing a message must stay in view in a narrow window, and a valid long name pushes Send out of reach, though only with an unusual unbroken name.
A cancel click that is silently dropped leaves the task running with no feedback, a real but timing-dependent cost to steering work.
Showing live progress and a pending reply while the server is down misleads a little, but a restart shows the right state and nothing is lost.
The request asks to return without losing my place, and losing the scroll position and an unsent draft on reload is a real but modest annoyance.
The request asks the bot to ask clarifying questions and follow up, yet answering its own clarifying question just echoes and drops the pending update, a plain defect in a core flow.
Without a way to clear active instructions the user cannot return a bot to no instructions short of making a new bot, a real gap in changing them as needs change.
The request wants each change stated exactly, and undelimited values can make a preview misleading, though only for values that contain separator-like text.
An update quietly rounds a huge total, inconsistent with the create flow's refusal, though the preview does show the rounded value and the input is extreme.
Silently cutting the end off an overlong message and sending it changes what the user said with no notice, though it takes over 12,000 characters.
The request says a refused token shows an alert, and an operator whose environment token is silently ignored cannot tell why setup reappeared.
